clue.text: Bounty from north, happily distributed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are spread about and dealt out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A windfall coming down from the north is gladly shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges NORTH plus HAPPILY, twelve letters in all; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounty is generosity or a generous gift, and philanthropy is charitable giving.

clue.text: Most of tablet horrible for the crusader

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: a tablet is a pill
grim means horrible

explanation.surface: Someone takes a nasty pill before setting off on crusade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last L of PILL to leave PIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader travelled to the Holy Land on a religious journey, like any pilgrim.

clue.text: Outbreak of rain in the country

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters things, so the four letters of rain burst into a new order

explanation.surface: A sudden shower falls somewhere in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outbreak of' rearranges RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: Fish and beer — the better half?

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
'my better half' is a jokey phrase for one's wife

explanation.surface: Asks whether fish and beer is the better half of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: An alewife is a North American fish of the herring family; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a species of herring found off the Atlantic coast of North America.

clue.text: On a sailing-ship salute takes an afternoon?

indicators.note: the toast takes in, or holds, the afternoon abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to toast someone is to salute them with a drink
PM stands for post meridiem, an afternoon time

explanation.surface: On board a sailing ship, a ceremonial salute lasts a whole afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is the container signal; the definition is loose, naming where a topmast is found rather than what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the upper section of a mast, a spar found aboard sailing vessels.

clue.text: Buck up and bring up

definitions.meaning: a bucking horse rises up on its hind legs
to bring up a child is to raise it

explanation.definitionFit: A horse that rears lifts itself upright as a bucking horse does, and to rear children is to raise them.

clue.text: Fee for umpire turning out to begin match?

indicators.note: turning out suggests the umpire's letters being turned over into a fresh shape
to begin a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Asks whether a payment is due to the umpire for coming out to start a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' rearranges UMPIRE into PREMIU; 'to begin' takes M from match; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A premium is a sum paid, such as an insurance charge or an extra fee.

clue.text: Dealing with Cook, perhaps, to provide a refuge for pedestrians

parts.note: traffic means dealing or trade, often illicit
Cook is one of the Cook Islands in the Pacific, so an example of an island

explanation.surface: Trading with Captain Cook offers a safe haven to people on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the explorer or a chef but is an island; 'with' and 'to provide a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic island is a raised spot in the road where people crossing can wait safely.

clue.text: But nettlerash can break out and cause a reversal!

indicators.note: a rash breaking out matches letters breaking out of their order into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Nettle rash may erupt and so undo all your plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break out' rearranges the thirteen letters of BUT NETTLERASH; 'can' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse one's position against an opponent, gaining the upper hand, is the idiom meant.

clue.text: Soldiers, with prospect of new life, make free

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers
a new lease of life is a fresh start, so lease is the word that phrase points to

explanation.surface: Troops given hope of a fresh start are set at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) plus LEASE from the idiom 'a new lease of life'; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone is to let them go, set at liberty.

clue.text: Table displaying dish tipped with gold

indicators.note: tipped with means the dish has the gold symbol attached at its end

parts.note: a plate is a dish
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A dining table shows off a gilt-rimmed dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' is not furniture but tableland; 'displaying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is tableland, a raised area of flat ground.

clue.text: Solid business

definitions.meaning: solid means steady and fixed in place

explanation.definitionFit: Firm means steady or unyielding, and a firm is also a company or commercial concern.

clue.text: Gold sovereign?

parts.note: not a coin: a king from Greek legend whose touch turned everything to gold

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Phrygian king had the golden touch, a monarch defined by gold.

clue.text: Sawyer's mate, fellow opening pub

indicators.note: the fellow's letter opens, or begins, the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Tom Sawyer's friend starts up a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Huckleberry Finn is Tom Sawyer's friend in Mark Twain's novels; Sawyer here is not a woodcutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Huckleberry, Tom Sawyer's sidekick in Twain's books, has this surname.

clue.text: Uses needles to make one row upside down

indicators.note: in a down entry, upside down reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: a stink is a row or fuss, as in to kick up a stink

explanation.surface: Someone knits a single row with the work turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' reverses STINK, a row or fuss; 'to make one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working with knitting needles to loop wool is knitting.

clue.text: Football team's bad player (but not at home)

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the team itself

indicators.note: not means the at-home letters are taken away

parts.note: a villain is the bad character in a play
in means at home

explanation.surface: A football side's poor performer is absent when the side plays at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad player' is not a weak footballer but the stage villain; Aston Villa is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa, a Birmingham club, is known simply as Villa.

clue.text: Huge chaps, semi-trained outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go outside, around, the word for chaps
trained suggests the letters being shaped and drilled into a new form

parts.note: men are chaps

explanation.surface: Big fellows, partly trained, are outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' gives IMSE, which 'outside' wraps around the chaps; 'semi' is not half but fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means vast or enormous, the same as huge.

clue.text: Pride of one in best suit, going to hospital?

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed in the word for best suit

parts.note: the trump suit is the strongest suit in a card game
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asks whether a man proud of his best suit is headed for hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best suit' means cards, not clothes; 'of' and 'going to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great success, a source of exultation and pride.

clue.text: Time's up, in a way, for catalyst

indicators.note: in a way here hints that the phrase's letters are rendered in a different form

explanation.surface: Running out of time spurs action in a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges the seven letters of TIME'S UP; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst is something that drives change, a driving force or stimulus.

clue.text: Head allowed in to see range of colours

indicators.note: in tells us the word for allowed is put inside the word for head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A headteacher lets someone in to view an array of colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is not a headteacher but the top of the skull; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's palette holds, and by extension names, a range of colours.

clue.text: Shrill cry, finding rock fragments by church

indicators.note: by means the church abbreviation is placed beside the rock word

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock on a slope

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks on finding loose stones beside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh, high scream.

clue.text: Sitting-bower?

parts.note: not a garden arbour to sit in: a musician who sits down and draws a bow

explanation.definitionFit: A player of the big string instrument sits to play and uses a bow.

clue.text: Primrose from Hereford's border?

parts.note: a Hereford is a breed of cow, so Hereford's gives cow's
a lip is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A primrose growing at the edge of Hereford.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford is a cattle breed, not just the English city; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild flower of the genus Primula, a kind of primrose.

clue.text: Be disposed to tip?

definitions.meaning: to be ... or minded to do something
to tip is to slope or lean

explanation.definitionFit: To feel inclined towards something is to lean that way, and a slope or tilt is also this word.

clue.text: Look left twice and lean against lamp-post, perhaps

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: twice means the letter for left is written two times

explanation.surface: Glance left two times and then slouch against a lamp-post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge or slump lazily, as one might against a post.

clue.text: Father confess and make headlines?

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: A priest admits something and gets into the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make headlines' is not news but lines on the forehead; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowling creases the forehead, putting lines on one's head.

clue.text: Blackleg, a disease of sheep?

definitions.meaning: a strike-breaker who works during a strike
a skin disease of sheep, a kind of mange

explanation.definitionFit: A strike-breaker is called a scab, and scab is also a skin disease of sheep.

clue.text: Some serve up gin

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: part means some

explanation.surface: A few people dish up gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PART; 'serve' is a link; gin here is a snare, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals.

clue.text: Silver-headed painter of Indian city

indicators.note: headed means the silver symbol comes at the head of the painter

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A grey-haired artist from a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra, home of the Taj Mahal, is a city in Uttar Pradesh.

clue.text: Bizarre shrub from nursery that inspired Infanta's visit?

definitions.text: from nursery that inspired Infanta's visit

parts.note: nut, as in nutty, suggests something crazy or bizarre
a tree is loosely a woody plant like a shrub

explanation.surface: An odd bush from a nursery rhyme brought a Spanish princess to call.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'I had a little nut tree' says the King of Spain's daughter came to visit; an Infanta is a Spanish princess.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, a little tree bearing a silver nutmeg draws the King of Spain's daughter.

clue.text: Brown coal left to catch fire

parts.note: to ignite is to catch fire

explanation.surface: Brown coal is left to burn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lignite is a soft brownish fuel ranked between peat and bituminous coal.

clue.text: Prevent strife in dungeon-the silence follows

indicators.note: follows means the silence word comes after what precedes it

parts.note: a keep is a castle's stronghold tower, often holding the dungeon
peace means silence

explanation.surface: Avoid conflict in a prison cell, where quiet comes after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain order and stop quarrels is the idiom meant.
